articles.title: 7 AI Tools That Can Plan Your Entire Week in One Prompt
articles.excerpt: Published: October 18, 2026 You know that feeling — it's Sunday evening, your plate is full, and the thought of mapping out Monday through Friday makes you want to close the laptop and stare at the ce…
articles.body: Published: October 18, 2026 You know that feeling — it's Sunday evening, your plate is full, and the thought of mapping out Monday through Friday makes you want to close the laptop and stare at the ceiling. What if you could just tell an AI what's on your plate and have it hand back a realistic, time-blocked week? That's no longer science fiction. Here are 7 tools that actually do this today — ranked by how close they get to the "one prompt, done week" fantasy.
articles.author: Bhargav Bhatt

articles.title: Seu LLM vai falhar e vai ser enganado: idempotência e segurança em fluxos de e-commerce
articles.excerpt: Imagine um e-commerce que resolveu colocar IA no atendimento. Nada de exótico: um agente lê a mensagem do cliente, consulta o pedido e, quando faz sentido, emite um cupom de desconto para compensar um…
articles.body: Imagine um e-commerce que resolveu colocar IA no atendimento. Nada de exótico: um agente lê a mensagem do cliente, consulta o pedido e, quando faz sentido, emite um cupom de desconto para compensar um atraso ou um produto que chegou errado. Menos fila para o time de suporte, resposta em segundos, cliente feliz. Nas primeiras semanas, tudo funciona. Até que o financeiro aparece com uma planilha: clientes recebendo dois cupons pelo mesmo problema . Um de 10% e outro de 15%, emitidos com poucos segundos de diferença, para o mesmo pedido. Nenhum erro no log que chamasse atenção. Nenhum alerta. O modelo não "enlouqueceu". O sistema fez exatamente o que foi programado para fazer: tentou de novo . E esse nem é o pior problema da história. Mas vamos por partes.
articles.author: Daniel Camucatto

articles.title: Twelve Hours Apart: Leading DoCheck's Engineering Team From the Other Side of the Planet
articles.excerpt: From 2021 to 2023 I was CTO of DoCheck, a productivity SaaS with a 20+ engineering team in Indonesia. I was in Orlando, finishing an M.S. in Computer Science at the University of Central Florida on a…
articles.body: From 2021 to 2023 I was CTO of DoCheck, a productivity SaaS with a 20+ engineering team in Indonesia. I was in Orlando, finishing an M.S. in Computer Science at the University of Central Florida on a Fulbright scholarship. Indonesia runs roughly twelve hours ahead of Florida. My team's afternoon was my middle of the night; their standup was my bedtime. No scheduling trick makes that go away. With a twelve-hour offset the only overlap you get is the overlap you deliberately buy, and you pay for it with somebody's evening. Velocity went up 30% over that period. Not because of the distance, but because the distance made it impossible to keep getting away with several things. The time zone audits your process A co-located team runs on ambient information. Someone overhears a decision.
articles.author: Faishal Wahiduddin

articles.title: Chrome 158 Drops XSLT on 17 November: Fix RSS and Sitemaps
articles.excerpt: On 17 November 2026, Chrome 158 stops running XSLT on Stable for everyone except Origin Trial and Enterprise Policy participants, so any RSS feed, Atom feed or XML sitemap that relies on an XSL styles…
articles.body: On 17 November 2026, Chrome 158 stops running XSLT on Stable for everyone except Origin Trial and Enterprise Policy participants, so any RSS feed, Atom feed or XML sitemap that relies on an XSL stylesheet will lose its styled browser view. [1] The XML itself still parses and still downloads. Feed readers and search engine crawlers read the data, not the stylesheet, so the damage is mostly to the page a human sees when they click your feed link. This post covers exactly which features are removed, which stay, a table of what breaks, and four fixes with code you can paste today.

When detectives have to sift through multi-page interrogation notes, vehicle tracking logs, and security footage, it takes hours to spot a lie. I wanted an AI app that could ingest these raw case files, map out the relationships, and instantly flag when a suspect's alibi falls apart. articles.excerpt: vLLM vs TGI vs Ollama: The Practical Guide to Serving and Running LLMs vLLM vs TGI vs Ollama: The Practical Guide to Serving and Running LLMs vLLM, Hugging Face Text Generation Inference (TGI), and Ol…
articles.body: vLLM vs TGI vs Ollama: The Practical Guide to Serving and Running LLMs vLLM vs TGI vs Ollama: The Practical Guide to Serving and Running LLMs Three different layers of the LLM stack vLLM, Hugging Face Text Generation Inference (TGI), and Ollama are frequently compared, but they sit at different points on the deployment spectrum. vLLM is optimized for high-throughput server-side inference. TGI is a production-grade model serving stack with strong Hugging Face ecosystem alignment. Ollama prioritizes local developer experience and model simplicity. The best choice depends on whether you are serving traffic at scale, running internal APIs, or experimenting locally on a laptop or workstation.

articles.title: DuckDB and Arrow Win AI Data Prep, Then Hit a Wall at Serving
articles.excerpt: TL;DR — Columnar engines like Arrow, DuckDB, Polars, and GPU dataframes are built for scan-heavy, amortized access — ideal for building training sets, terrible for single-row inference lookups. The re…
articles.body: TL;DR — Columnar engines like Arrow, DuckDB, Polars, and GPU dataframes are built for scan-heavy, amortized access — ideal for building training sets, terrible for single-row inference lookups. The real value of Arrow in AI systems isn't query speed, it's zero-copy interchange between the offline columnar world and the online row-oriented world. Teams that try to make one engine do both pay for it in p99 latency. Every few months another benchmark lands showing DuckDB or Polars or a GPU dataframe engine crushing some TPC-H-style workload. The numbers are real. The conclusion people draw from them — that the columnar engine is now the obvious backbone for AI data infrastructure, end to end — is where things go wrong.

articles.title: Astronomers want your help finding 'missing' black holes in the Milky Way
articles.excerpt: A citizen science project is seeking volunteers to comb through NASA telescope data for telltale signs of the galaxy's hidden black holes.
articles.body: Astronomers estimate that our home galaxy, the Milky Way, has churned out more than 10 million black holes over its 13-billion-year history. Yet so far, they have found only 70. Now, a group of astronomers in the U.K. is trying to close that vast gap by enlisting the public. Their project, called Black Hole Hunters , is looking for volunteers with a computer and a few spare minutes to sift through troves of data gathered by a NASA space telescope. By flagging recognizable patterns that could point to a "missing" black hole , volunteers can help fast-track a search that would otherwise take years, the team says.

articles.excerpt: FromSoft’s Echo Night asks players to bring peace to the dead.
articles.body: To trace FromSoftware’s history is to uncover a lineage written in cold sweat. While the studio is celebrated today for unforgiving action RPGs like Dark Souls and Elden Ring , its DNA is deeply rooted in games that feel born of a fever dream. FromSoft’s darker legacy lives in games like Kuon , a masterclass in Japanese folklore and survival horror, and Shadow Tower , a claustrophobic dungeon crawler that turns every dark alcove into a deadly trap. Even Eternal Ring — not to be confused with its blockbuster sibling Elden Ring — radiates that signature, unsettling aura that makes exploring FromSoftware’s later worlds so intoxicating.

articles.excerpt: From the Costa del Sol to whitewashed mountain villages, here are 10 of the best places in southern Spain to experience the Aug. 2, 2027 total solar eclipse.
articles.body: Spain is one of the easiest places in the world to experience the total solar eclipse on Aug. 2, 2027 . The so-called "eclipse of the century" first makes landfall in Andalucía, where totality will last up to 4 minutes and 40 seconds during mid-morning, with the sun comfortably high at around 38-42 degrees above the horizon in the eastern sky. Excellent roads, plentiful accommodation and Málaga's international airport make this an obvious alternative to North Africa and the Middle East. However, choosing where to watch requires some thought.

articles.title: 'Let's all choose to make tomorrow better', Artemis II astronauts honored with Stephen Hawking Medal at Starmus
articles.excerpt: The Artemis II crew have joined an impressive list of honourees, including Buzz Aldrin, Jane Goodall and David Attenborough.
articles.body: TENERIFE, CANARY ISLANDS — The Artemis II astronauts may have traveled hundreds of thousands of miles away from Earth to the moon, but they made sure the rest of us didn't miss out on the adventure. Now, their efforts to bring the wonders of space exploration back down to Earth have earned them one of science communication's most prestigious honors: the Stephen Hawking Medal. NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman and Victor Glover , alongside Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen , accepted the award on Saturday (Oct. 17), during the opening ceremony of the Starmus VIII festival. The honor recognizes all four crew members, including NASA astronaut Christina Koch , who wasn't in attendance.

articles.body: Lucy’s quote, “Happiness is a warm puppy,” is another great one that touches on life’s simple joys on a really deep level. But to determine the best quote ever uttered by Charlie Brown, I didn't want accidental brilliance, I wanted something that he understands as much as the audience does. Something where he’s telling you who he is with complete self awareness. I wanted the character's philosophy on life. To me, that’s the difference between a brilliant Charlie Brown quote and brilliant Charles Schulz quote, if that makes sense.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 17, 2016: Private Antares rocket returns to flight after catastrophic launch explosion
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 17, 2016, the Antares rocket now built by Northrop Grumman Space Systems returned to flight to come back from a catastrophic explosion. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 17, 2016, Orbital ATK (now Northrop Grumman Space Systems ) returned to flight, successfully launching a cargo shipment to the International Space Station (ISS) after its previous cargo mission failed to launch. The private spaceflight company was contracted by NASA to fly cargo to the ISS, and stakes were high for this launch. Orbital ATK's last attempt nearly two years earlier ended in a catastrophic explosion a few seconds after liftoff. Despite some delays, the newly upgraded Antares rocket flawlessly blasted off into the night sky from NASA's Wallops Flight Facility in Virginia. Six days later, the Cygnus cargo spacecraft arrived at the ISS to deliver food, supplies and science experiments to the crew.

articles.title: This Week In Space podcast: Episode 232 — The Lunar Dump
articles.excerpt: On Episode 232 of This Week In Space, Rod Pyle and Tariq Malik are joined by Chelsea Gohd to talk about the recent large data dump from the Artemis II mission.
articles.body: On Episode 232 of This Week In Space , Rod Pyle and Tariq Malik are joined by Chelsea Gohd, former writer for NASA/JPL and now with Space.com, to talk about the recent large data dump from the Artemis II mission. What was included? Why is this new data important? What observations were made, and what discoveries might result from them? What kind of annotations and notes did the astronauts include that make these observations uniquely valuable? articles.title: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites
articles.excerpt: The actions could have resulted in criminal charges had humans been behind the keyboard.
articles.body: OpenAI said internal models hacked two more websites, bypassed company-imposed browsing restrictions, and used exposed credentials to draw cryptocurrency from a wallet it couldn’t otherwise access, in the latest installment of disclosures of its agents performing unethical and likely illegal acts. The company on Thursday issued reports of four new incidents, all of which occurred in June. They come after the company revealed in July that internal test agents exploited a zero-day vulnerability in a tool designed to restrict their access to the Internet. They then broke into the network of AI tool provider Hugging Face. The agents took that illegal action to steal answers to a hacking test that weren’t available when completing the tasks on their own.
